'''Lincoln Red Imps Football Club''' is a professional [[association football|football]] club from [[Gibraltar]].<ref>{{Cite news|last=Brookfield|first=Saul|date=2016-07-12|title=Lincoln Red Imps, the Gibraltar part-timers who embarrassed Celtic|language=en-GB|work=The Guardian|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2016/jul/12/lincoln-red-imps-gibraltar-celtic|access-date=2020-05-12|issn=0261-3077|archive-date=28 March 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200328063051/https://www.theguardian.com/football/2016/jul/12/lincoln-red-imps-gibraltar-celtic|url-status=live}}</ref> They play in the [[Gibraltar Football League]], and share [[Victoria Stadium, Gibraltar|Victoria Stadium]] with all other clubs in the territory.<ref>{{cite web|title=Lincoln Red Imps|url=https://www.uefa.com/nationalassociations/teams/2605572--l-red-imps/|website=[[UEFA]]|access-date=13 May 2019|archive-date=31 January 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200131215932/https://www.uefa.com/teamsandplayers/teams/club%3D2605572/profile/index.html|url-status=live}}</ref> They are the country's record champion with 29 league titles, including fourteen consecutive titles between 2003 and 2016, and in 2014 were the first team to represent Gibraltar in the [[UEFA Champions League]]'s qualifying stage. In August 2021, Lincoln became the first club from Gibraltar to ever reach the group stages of a European club competition after defeating the Latvian champions [[Riga FC]] in the play-off round of the [[2021–22 UEFA Europa Conference League|UEFA Europa Conference League]]. 

The club has won 7 [[domestic treble]]s and 4 [[Double (association football)|doubles]] in its history.<ref>{{Cite web |title=OUR STORY SO FAR |url=https://lincolnredimpsfc.co.uk/clubinfo/our-story-so-far |access-date=2024-02-26 |website=lincolnredimpsfc.co.uk |language=en}}</ref> They hold the record for Europe's longest men's chronological unbeaten league run of 88 matches over 1,959 days from May 2009 to September 2014.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/51692518|title=Where did Liverpool's run rank with greats?|work=BBC Sport|access-date=1 March 2020|archive-date=4 March 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200304181633/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/51692518|url-status=live}}</ref>"}}
